ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A and B are the intersections of the inverse proportion function $y_{1} = \frac{10}{x}$ and the linear function $y=2x$. Point C is on the inverse proportion function $y_{2} = \frac{k}{x}$. Connect OC, draw $AD \perp x$-axis through point A to intersect OC at point D, and connect BD. If $AD=BD$ and $OC=3OD$, then what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Solve the system of equations $\begin{cases}y=2x\\ y=\frac{10}{x}\end{cases}$,\\
we get $\begin{cases}x_{1}=-\sqrt{5}\\ y_{1}=-2\sqrt{5}\end{cases}$, $\begin{cases}x_{2}=\sqrt{5}\\ y_{2}=2\sqrt{5}\end{cases}$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point A are ($-\sqrt{5}$, $-2\sqrt{5}$), and the coordinates of point B are ($\sqrt{5}$, $2\sqrt{5}$),\\
$\because$ A and B are symmetric about the origin,\\
$\therefore$ O is the midpoint of AB,\\
also, $\because$ AD = BD,\\
$\therefore$ point D lies on the perpendicular bisector of segment AB,\\
$\therefore$ CO$\perp$AB,\\
also, $\because$ AH$\perp$x-axis,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOH + $\angle$OAH = $\angle$AOH + $\angle$COH = $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OAH = $\angle$COH,\\
draw CE$\perp$x-axis at point E,\\
$\because$ OC = 3OD, and the x-coordinate of point D is $-\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ the x-coordinate of point C is $-3\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\because \tan \angle$OAH = $\tan \angle$COH = $\frac{OH}{AH}$ = $\frac{CE}{OE}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ CE = $\frac{1}{2}$OE = $\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point C are ($-3\sqrt{5}$, $\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}$),\\
$\therefore$ k = $-3\sqrt{5} \times \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}$ = $\boxed{-\frac{45}{2}}$.

From the image, read that A is the lower-left intersection and B is the upper-right intersection, AD is the vertical segment through A meeting OC at D, and D lies on the same ray from O toward C with C farther out. From the text, use A,B as intersections of y=10/x and y=2x, so A=(-sqrt(5),-2sqrt(5)) and B=(sqrt(5),2sqrt(5)). Since AD is vertical, write D=(-sqrt(5),t). Use the given AD=BD directly as a distance equation: (t+2sqrt(5))^2 = (t-2sqrt(5))^2 + ( -sqrt(5)-sqrt(5) )^2, solve t=sqrt(5)/2. Then D=(-sqrt(5),sqrt(5)/2). Because O,D,C are collinear and the image/text indicate OC=3OD with C beyond D on ray OD, take C=3D=(-3sqrt(5),3sqrt(5)/2). Since C lies on y=k/x, compute k=x_C y_C = -45/2.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中有坐标轴，原点为 O；A 是直线与反比例函数在第三象限的交点，位置在左下方；B 是对应在第一象限的交点，位置在右上方。过 A 作的 AD 是一条竖直线段，与从 O 指向左上方 C 的线段 OC 相交于 D；图中 D 位于 O 到 C 的同一射线上，且 C 在 D 的更外侧；还连接了 B 与 D。

再推理：A、B 是 y=10/x 与 y=2x 的交点。由 2x=10/x，得 2x^2=10，所以 x^2=5，x=±√5。对应 y=2x，因此按图中位置，A=(-√5,-2√5)，B=(√5,2√5)。

因为 AD 是过 A 的竖直线，所以 D 的 x 坐标与 A 相同，可设 D=(-√5,t)。由 AD=BD，列距离方程：AD^2=(t+2√5)^2；BD^2=(-√5-√5)^2+(t-2√5)^2=20+(t-2√5)^2。因此 (t+2√5)^2=20+(t-2√5)^2。展开化简得 t=√5/2，所以 D=(-√5,√5/2)。

又因为 O、D、C 共线，且图中 C 在从 O 经 D 延长的同一射线上，并且 OC=3OD，所以 C=3D=(-3√5,3√5/2)。点 C 在 y=k/x 上，因此 k=x_C y_C=(-3√5)(3√5/2)=-45/2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, points A and B are the intersections of the inverse proportion function $y_{1}=\frac{10}{x}$ and the linear function $y=2x$. Point C is on the inverse proportion function $y_{2}=\frac{k}{x}$. Connect OC, draw $AD\perp x$-axis through point A to intersect OC at point D, and connect BD. If $AD=BD$ and $OC=3OD$, then what is the value of $k$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Solve the system of equations $\begin{cases}y=2x\\ y=\frac{10}{x}\end{cases}$,\\
we get $\begin{cases}x_{1}=-\sqrt{5}\\ y_{1}=-2\sqrt{5}\end{cases}$, $\begin{cases}x_{2}=\sqrt{5}\\ y_{2}=2\sqrt{5}\end{cases}$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point A are ($-\sqrt{5}$, $-2\sqrt{5}$), and the coordinates of point B are ($\sqrt{5}$, $2\sqrt{5}$),\\
$\because$ A and B are symmetric about the origin,\\
$\therefore$ O is the midpoint of AB,\\
also, $\because$ AD = BD,\\
$\therefore$ point D lies on the perpendicular bisector of segment AB,\\
$\therefore$ CO$\perp$AB,\\
also, $\because$ AH$\perp$x-axis,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOH + $\angle$OAH = $\angle$AOH + $\angle$COH = $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OAH = $\angle$COH,\\
draw CE$\perp$x-axis at point E,\\
$\because$ OC = 3OD, and the x-coordinate of point D is $-\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ the x-coordinate of point C is $-3\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\because \tan \angle$OAH = $\tan \angle$COH = $\frac{OH}{AH}$ = $\frac{CE}{OE}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ CE = $\frac{1}{2}$OE = $\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point C are ($-3\sqrt{5}$, $\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}$),\\
$\therefore$ k = $-3\sqrt{5} \times \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}$ = $\boxed{-\frac{45}{2}}$
